finding.text: `Servex/doc/processes.md` (new "Coverage" section, gap 2) says "`pid-coverage.mjs`'s companion check of every live `claude.exe` against every logged pid found none unlogged", but `Servex/pid-coverage.mjs` has no such check: it only reads log lines. Either add the check or reword it as a one-off manual check made on 2026-11-08.

The same section says claude.exe lines "end and attribute near 100%", but the measured end rate is 81.8% (report.md table; a rerun now gives 82.4%, 28/34). Its snapshot count (1,460 starts) also differs from report.md's 1,478. Quote the real numbers, and say whether the 6 open claude.exe starts are live agents or missed ends.
`pid-coverage.mjs` is not indexed: `Servex/readme.md:51` lists `Lineage.js` and `leaks.mjs` but not the new `pid-coverage.mjs` or its test.

report.md is stale against the branch. It says "commit `08d1c600f`" and "`Servex/pid-coverage-report.md` is the committed output", but the branch head `beec66a38` deletes that file ("drop the snapshot file"). The brief asked for the output file to be committed. Either restore it or correct report.md to name `beec66a38` and say the table lives only in report.md.

`Servex/doc/processes.md` still quotes the old heading, "Fallback when Servex is down", which the same diff renames to "Fallback ONLY when Servex itself cannot be reached" (`Servex/agents/roles/mastermind.md:60`).

The header comment in `Servex/pid-coverage.mjs:2` says rows are sorted "by its `cmd`/`why` text", but `kind_of()` deliberately ignores `why`, as the comment at its line 25 explains. The header should say `cmd` only.

`kind_of()` files any `chrome.exe` under "chrome (playwright)". That is safe here, since only lines we logged are counted, but the label claims more than the code checks. Given the owner's rule about killing Chrome, nobody should reuse this classifier to pick kill targets.

The fix rewords the fallback rather than removing it or logging the launch. That is a reasonable small choice, and the alternative is recorded. Other docs still present `claude -p` as a way to start minions, though (`public/framework/ai/handoff2.md:47`, `public/framework/ai/doc/agent-context.md:23`). A mastermind reading those could take the same bypass.
The task log (`session.jsonl` here) has a summary log line and commits but no landing or outcome line. A fresh agent can continue from report.md, but the task does not read as closed.

The sweep breaks the single-writer rule. `Servex.js:355` (branch `worktree/pid-gone-ends`, 5b6f711d4) runs `leaks.mjs --close-gone` as a separate child process. In that child `LogLine.writer` is never set, so `LogLine.raw` (`Server/LogLine.mjs:57`) and the direct `fs.appendFileSync` to `spawns.jsonl` (`Servex/leaks.mjs`, `--close-gone` branch) both append to session logs that Servex itself is writing pid lines into at that moment. The fix: have the child print its `writes` as JSON (the `--dry-run` output plus the lines) and let Servex append them through `this.log` / `SpawnLog.sink`.

The task folder doesn't know this change exists. `report.md` §1 still says the 4 gone claude.exe starts were "not investigated further", and §4 names only 08d1c600f/beec66a38. The task's `session.jsonl` already has its `complete` line. The new commit and its branch are recorded only in the parent's log (`mastermind-resources/session.jsonl:607`). A fresh agent working from this folder would not know that `worktree/pid-gone-ends` exists, is unmerged, and needs this review. Add a §6 (or a log line plus a report update) naming the commit, the branch and its merge state.

The header comment at `Servex/leaks.mjs:7` still says "It only READS", and the very next added lines describe a write. The `Servex/readme.md:51` row still calls `leaks.mjs` "the report". Both should mention `--close-gone`.

A backfilled `"seen":"boot"` end counts as a real end in `pid-coverage.mjs`. After the first boot sweep, claude.exe's "with end" will read close to 100% and hide the crash gap this task measured. Count `seen:"boot"` ends as their own column, or say in `doc/processes.md` that the end % includes them.
In `Servex/leaks.test.mjs` (end of the file) the new `close_lines()` checks run after the line `leaks.test: all checks pass` has already printed. Move that line to the end.

The fix itself is sound and small, and its test passes. `close_lines()` respects `pair()`'s window, since `ended` lands in `[s.t, next)`, and the new test proves that `pair()` then treats the start as closed. Each boot writes lines only for gone starts that have no end yet, so the sweep is idempotent. The first boot will backfill every historic gone start (about 38 all time), appending to old, landed session logs. That is append-only, so it is acceptable, but worth knowing.
